fun_facts: Patrick Mahomes grew up in Tyler, Texas.
As a kid, Patrick Mahomes mostly played baseball and basketball; he started playing football in seventh grade.
In high school, Patrick Mahomes pitched a no-hitter and struck out 16 batters.
At Texas Tech, Patrick Mahomes led the FBS in passing yards in 2016.
Patrick Mahomes has been called “Showtime Mahomes.”
At age 24 years and 138 days, Patrick Mahomes became the youngest quarterback to win Super Bowl MVP; he also led three double-digit comebacks in one postseason, a first for an NFL quarterback.

basis.reasoning: The ESPN biography lists Patrick Mahomes's college as Texas Tech, supporting the answer.

You look at Dak, he did not expect to start immediately, but he really trained so he was gonna be ready when the time came and it did.

**I didn't do any football stuff when I was a kid.** ... Mostly baseball and basketball the whole time. That's all I did. I played football starting in seventh grade. As I got older, I started playing a little bit more. Then in high school, I really fell in love with it.

excerpts:
And now I have and I'm here -- it's amazing.

"When I won the game and they came up and told me [I'd won the MVP], it was amazing -- just to be able to say those words and to be here now. ... I tried to dream it, and I tweeted it, and I kinda spoke it into existence."

At the time of his tweet, Mahomes was a multisport athlete in Tyler, Texas, trying to decide what he wanted to do next. His father, Pat Mahomes Sr., was a Major League Baseball pitcher for 11 seasons and tried to talk his son into quitting football so he could focus on baseball, in which he pitched a no-hitter with 16 strikeouts in high school. In football, Mahomes wasn't listed among ESPN's top 300 football recruits.

But he chose to follow his passion, which he acknowledged wasn't easy.

"I was never that kid [to go against my parents]," Mahomes told ESPN. "To me it was just, 'Let's just go try this football thing out. Let's go to college and play it.

excerpts: Mahomes became the youngest quarterback to be named Super Bowl MVP, joining [Tom Brady](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/2330/tom-brady) as the only ones to do so before turning 25. Mahomes is the third-youngest Super Bowl MVP overall, trailing only [Marcus Allen](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3116149/marcus-allen) and Lynn Swann. He also became the youngest quarterback in NFL history, at 24 years and 138 days, to win a Super Bowl and league MVP (2018).
